candidate.title: PBAT
candidate.scope: The assigned PBAT (post-bisulfite adaptor tagging) row, specifically the two-round random-primer, biotin-streptavidin capture implementation described by Miura et al. (2012). This is a whole-genome bisulfite library architecture: conversion precedes adapter tagging, followed by first-strand capture, second random priming and synthesis, and elution to adapter-tagged DNA. The nearby Bisulfite-Seq/WGBS, EpiGnome/HELP-Seq and BSPP rows are separate contextual workflows; the repeated methylation icon at the left names the PBAT concept rather than adding a transformation or parallel branch. The verified secondary page is headed PBAT and reproduces this route; its single-cell and application references do not expand the target. Sequencing, size selection and analysis settings are not separately drawn operations.

states.label: Eluted DNA library with adapters
features: The poster endpoint is labeled DNA with adaptors and is represented by one blue line with orange and magenta terminal adapter segments, separated from the bead.

The primary implementation releases second-strand DNA and makes the eluted library double stranded while completing the sequence required for Illumina bridge PCR; the endpoint is not interpreted as a definitively single-stranded finished library.
The readout carrier is newly synthesized adapter-tagged genomic DNA copies carrying bisulfite conversion information, not the original methylated molecules or the beads.
Primary-paper reads are generally G-poor because sequencing reads the complement of converted C-poor DNA; occasional C-poor reads are also reported.

The library supports genome-wide methylation inference at single-base resolution for represented, interpretable sites. Bisulfite-resistant signal does not distinguish 5mC from 5hmC, and random priming can bias representation.

Conversion lowers sequence complexity and can obscure C/T sequence variation; methylation is inferred from conversion-aware sequence comparison at interpretable genomic sites, not from the adapter or biotin itself.

operations.label: Bisulfite conversion
operations.description: Treat the genomic DNA before attaching adapters, producing conversion-encoded, fragmented genomic templates for first-strand synthesis.
operations.mechanism: Bisulfite treatment changes the sequence readout of susceptible unmethylated cytosines and can break DNA. PBAT postpones adapter addition until after this treatment, avoiding subsequent bisulfite damage to an already adapter-tagged library.
operations.information_effect: Genomic location and cytosine modification status become recoverable from sequence and conversion outcomes after copying. The assay does not intrinsically resolve 5mC from 5hmC.

operations.label: First random priming
operations.description: Anneal the first adapter-bearing random primer to converted genomic fragments and extend it to synthesize a complementary first DNA strand. The product gains a primer-derived adapter and a 5′ biotin capture handle.
operations.mechanism: Random primer extension generates adapter-tagged copies directly on bisulfite-treated DNA. The primary primer has 5′ biotin and 3′ N4; polymerase extends its annealed 3′ end.
operations.information_effect: Converted genomic sequence information is copied into the first strand, physically linked to the first adapter and capture handle. Random priming selects represented fragments and may introduce site preferences.

operations.label: Capture first strand on Streptavidin-coated magnetic beads
operations.description: Capture the biotinylated first-strand product on streptavidin beads. The diagram continues with an immobilized first strand; the primary protocol clarifies that denaturation separates the original converted template.

operations.information_effect: The captured object is the first DNA copy, not a methylation-specific pull-down of the original genomic molecule. The bead preserves that copy as a template through subsequent synthesis.

operations.label: Elution
operations.description: Release second-strand DNA from the bead-associated product to yield DNA with adaptors. The poster compresses this into one arrow; the primary implementation also makes the eluted DNA double stranded and completes the bridge-PCR sequence within its elution stage.
operations.mechanism: Primary-paper elution separates the second strand from the biotin-retained first-strand template and uses primer extension to produce the completed double-stranded sequencing template. No global library PCR amplification is shown or required in the matched implementation.
operations.information_effect: The resulting adapter-tagged DNA can supply Illumina methylation reads. In the reported orientation, reads generally complement converted C-poor DNA and are G-poor; occasional opposite-orientation reads are reported. Methylation inference is limited by conversion specificity, fragment representation and priming bias; completed bridge-PCR sequence is a sequencing interface, not evidence of global library amplification.

method_scopes.rationale: PBAT and its expansion Post-bisulfite adaptor tagging denote one target here. All six local operations belong to the single arrow-connected PBAT row. The poster reference matches Miura et al. 2012 (PMID 22649061), whose inspected full text specifies this biotinylated first primer, capture, second N4 primer and amplification-free sequencing-template implementation. This resolves applicability to the depicted implementation without asserting that every use of the broader PBAT strategy has identical preparation. No split, pooling, or alternative PBAT workflow is depicted. The additional citations on the secondary catalogue page were inspected only as catalogue listings: Smallwood et al. (2014) concerns single-cell bisulfite sequencing; Guo et al. (2015) and Sakashita et al. (2015) are described as PBAT applications; Yong et al. (2016) is a broad review. Their primary texts were not supplied or inspected, so they are background at this scope and are not used as primary architecture evidence. The registered publication and literal method-reference sources concern Miura et al. (2012), assessed in pm_miura2012.

corrections.diagram_observation: The PBAT endpoint DNA with adaptors is drawn as a single blue horizontal line with orange and magenta terminal segments after an arrow labeled Elution. The drawing does not specify the full strand-completion chemistry of this endpoint.
corrections.primary_statement: Miura et al. b00035 identifies the released molecule as second-strand DNA. Materials and methods b00019 explicitly states that the elution stage makes the DNA double stranded and synthesizes the sequence required for bridge PCR. The final state and Elution operation therefore describe a completed double-stranded sequencing library while retaining the simplified single-line depiction as the image observation. This resolves a compressed schematic interface, rather than treating the icon as proof of an exclusively single-stranded finished library.
